```{r}
library(SIGA)
```

## Simulation models

The simulation study of the SIGA paper (section 3) uses six models with 20
covariates and a binary treatment $Z$: two null models without a predictive
subgroup and four models with one.

| Model | Linear predictor $L$ | Prognostic | Predictive | True subgroup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | $0$ | none | none | none |
| A2 | $2(x_1 + x_2)$ | $x_1, x_2$ | none | none |
| B1 | $0.1(x_1 + x_2) + 2 Z I(x_4 > 1)$ | $x_1, x_2$ | $x_4$ | $x_4 > 1$ |
| B2 | $0.2(x_1 + x_2) + 1.2 Z I(x_1 > 0)$ | $x_1, x_2$ | $x_1$ | $x_1 > 0$ |
| B3 | $0.3(x_2 + x_9) + 2 Z I(x_4 > 1, x_5 = 1)$ | $x_2, x_9$ | $x_4, x_5$ | $x_4 > 1, x_5 = 1$ |
| B4 | $2 Z I(x_1 < 0.5, x_5 = 1, x_6 = 1)$ | none | $x_1, x_5, x_6$ | $x_1 < 0.5, x_5 = 1, x_6 = 1$ |

Survival times follow $T = 1.2\,(-\log U \, e^{L})^{1/4.34}$, so that the hazard
is proportional to $e^{-L}$ (a hazard ratio of $e^{-2} \approx 0.14$ in the B1
subgroup), and censoring times are uniform on $(0, \pi)$ with the values of
$\pi$ of the paper that give 30% censoring. `siga_simulate()` generates these
data; `siga_true_subgroup()` gives the true subgroup membership.

```{r}
d <- siga_simulate(600, model = "B4", seed = 1)
c(censoring = mean(d$status == 0), true_subgroup = mean(attr(d, "true_subgroup")))
```

The observed time is $\min(T, C)$, as described in the paper. `legacy = TRUE`
reproduces the original simulation program exactly for a given seed, including
two details that differ from the paper: the noise covariates
$x_{11}, \dots, x_{20}$ have pairwise correlation 0.5 within the block
(`noise_rho`), and the event time is stored as the observed time of censored
patients (the event indicator is correct). Censored patients then stay in the
risk sets until their event time. The Cox model remains valid, because
censoring does not depend on the covariates, but the risk sets are larger,
which can change the operating characteristics of SIGA. The validation chapter
of the user manual therefore uses proper censoring and compares the results
with those on data from the original program.

## Performance criteria

For every trial a training set $L_1$ ($n = 300$ or 600) and a test set $L_2$
($n = 5000$) are generated. SIGA is applied to $L_1$, and the subgroup found
is evaluated as follows:

* **false discovery rate** (A1, A2): proportion of trials with a subgroup;
* $p_{one}$, $p_{all}$, $p_{exact}$: probability that the subgroup uses at least
  one, all, or exactly the predictive biomarkers, given that a subgroup is
  found;
* **sensitivity, specificity, AUC**: classification of the $L_2$ patients into
  the true subgroup (AUC = (sensitivity + specificity) / 2 for a rule);
* subgroup proportion in $L_2$, hazard ratio of the subgroup in $L_1$ and in
  $L_2$, and the relative bias $(\hat\tau_{L_1} - \hat\tau_{L_2}) / \hat\tau_{L_2}$.

## Running a trial

One trial with the settings of the simulation study of the paper, which are
the package defaults (20 covariates, $k = 10$ candidates, $q = 10$ resamples,
$m = 50$, $MaxG = 50$ and $s = 5$ sub-populations in every resample and in the
final search):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
one_trial <- function(model, n, seed) {
  L1 <- siga_simulate(n, model, seed = seed)
  L2 <- siga_simulate(5000, model, seed = seed + 5)
  fit <- siga(Surv(time, status) ~ trt | ., data = L1, eta = 0.2, theta = 0.5,
              seed = seed, verbose = FALSE)
  if (!fit$subgroup) return(c(found = 0))
  pred <- predict(fit, L2)
  truth <- attr(L2, "true_subgroup")
  vars <- rule_variables(fit$rule)
  c(found = 1, all = all(attr(L1, "predictive") %in% vars),
    se = mean(pred[truth]), sp = mean(!pred[!truth]),
    hr_L2 = subgroup_effect(fit, data = L2)$table$estimate[2])
}
one_trial("B3", 300, seed = 1)
```

The validation scripts in the `validation/` directory of the source repository
run all scenarios in parallel (one resampling per trial, re-used for the nine
combinations of $\eta \in \{0.15, 0.2, 0.25\}$ and $\theta \in \{0.5, 0.7, 0.9\}$
with `update()`) and compare the results with Tables 3 to 6 of the paper. A
trial takes about half a minute on one core.
